validate_code statically validates Python source before sandbox execution in two layers. Layer 1 scans the raw string for blocked patterns using a word-boundary regex to avoid false positives. Layer 2 parses the code with ast.parse (SyntaxError becomes a SandboxViolation) and walks all nodes, blocking non-allowlisted imports and from-imports, calls to eval/exec/compile and __import__, dangerous dunder attribute access, and blocked builtin names. Input: a code string. Output: a list of non-fatal warnings (always empty in this implementation). Raises SandboxViolation on the first hard block. Edge cases: empty code and safe code pass; attribute-vs-name checks distinguish node types. validate_code performs pre-execution sandbox validation in two layers. First a fast regex string scan over BLOCKED_STR_PATTERNS with a negative lookbehind word boundary; then an AST walk that rejects imports not in ALLOWED_MODULES, dangerous calls (eval, exec, compile, __import__), dangerous dunder attributes, and blocked names. It returns a list of warnings (non-fatal) and raises SandboxViolation on any hard block, converting SyntaxError into a violation. Edge cases: empty input, safe code, and distinguishing attribute access from bare names. _extract_yarn_lock parses a yarn.lock file, supporting v1, v2 and berry v10 formats. It reads line by line, treating non-indented lines ending in colon as block keys, then captures the following version line. A nested flush helper emits a ManifestEntry (npm ecosystem, normalized name, version, lockfile source, line number) only when both key and version were seen. Aliased packages are handled: when a resolution line contains npm: and its name differs from the block key, the resolution name becomes the real package name. Inputs: text and source label; output: a list of ManifestEntry. Edge cases: blank lines and __metadata are skipped; quoted keys are unquoted; blocks without a version are dropped.
